questions.q: Why is `quantity * unit_price` calculated inside the SUM(), per row, rather than after aggregating each column separately?
options: GROUP BY requires all calculations to happen before aggregation for syntax reasons only
Per-row calculations run faster than aggregate calculations in Athena
Athena does not support multiplication between two columns
SUM(quantity) * SUM(unit_price) is a different, incorrect calculation than SUM(quantity * unit_price), and would silently produce the wrong revenue
questions.explain: Multiplying the totals of two already-summed columns is mathematically different from summing each row's product — the per-row version is the correct one.

questions.q: What does `GROUP BY product_category` actually do in this query?
options: Sorts the result alphabetically by category name
Creates a new table named product_category in the Glue Catalog
Filters out any row where product_category is missing
Collapses every individual order line into one summary row per product category
questions.explain: GROUP BY defines the grain of the aggregation — here, one row of totals per category.

questions.q: What does the real result reveal about Camp Kitchen vs. Tents & Shelters?
options: Tents & Shelters sold the most units and also earned the most revenue
Neither category had meaningfully different results from the others
Camp Kitchen sold the most units, but Tents & Shelters earned the most revenue — two different, both valid, answers to "sold the most"
Camp Kitchen won on both units and revenue
questions.explain: This is exactly why the question was clarified in Lesson 1 to require both units and revenue — a single metric would have hidden one of these two stories.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend spot-checking one category's total against a few raw rows by hand?
options: Aggregation bugs are invisible until checked — a quick manual sanity check catches mistakes before they reach the stakeholder
The Glue Crawler does not guarantee accurate row counts
SQL aggregate functions are known to be unreliable in Athena specifically
Athena requires manual verification before any query result can be trusted by law
questions.explain: A quick manual spot-check is good practice for any aggregation, since a subtly wrong formula can produce a plausible-looking but incorrect number.

questions.q: What does `ORDER BY total_units DESC` accomplish in this query?
options: Groups categories by region instead of by product line
Puts the category that sold the most units at the top of the result, directly answering half of the stakeholder's question
Filters out all categories except the single top seller
Converts total_units from a count into a percentage of all sales
questions.explain: Sorting descending by total_units surfaces the top-selling category by volume immediately, without needing to scan the whole result.
